name: Navratan Korma
subtitle: nine jewels: mixed vegetables, paneer, nuts and fruit in a pale sweet cream gravy
prepNotes: Navratan means nine gems, and the count is the point: vegetables, paneer, nuts and dried fruit should all be identifiable.
No tomato and no chilli powder. The gravy is deliberately pale and mild; heat belongs in a different dish.

steps.text: Boil the onion, ginger, cardamom and soaked cashews in 200ml water for 12 minutes, then blend to a smooth white paste.
Blanch the carrot, beans, cauliflower and potato until just tender and refresh in cold water so they keep their colour.
steps.tip: Refreshing matters. Vegetables left to sit hot go grey.

steps.text: Fry the paneer cubes in ghee until pale gold and set aside.
Cook the white paste in the remaining ghee for 8 minutes without letting it colour.
steps.tip: It must not brown. The colour of this dish is its signature.

steps.text: Add the milk, sugar and salt, and simmer to a coating consistency.
Fold in the vegetables, paneer, almonds and raisins and warm through for 4 minutes.
Finish off the heat with the cream and garam masala, and scatter pomegranate over.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. The cream can split on hard reheating, so warm it gently. Do not freeze.
